header.boundary: The card prioritizes and sizes the test. The live test decides. Moot Court never touches a ship, allocation or stopping rule.
header.test_count_definition: Tests in the ledger are the distinct test ids of every row of the source whatever its status. Tests admitted are the distinct test ids with at least one admitted contrast. Tests scored are the admitted tests with at least one contrast scored by the primary rung. The difference between admitted and scored is the contrasts of the first quarters, before the first origin with enough visible rows to fit (they are history only), plus any test whose contrasts all fall there.

gate_interval.dependence: per base rate in by_base_rate: rows per test and the binary within-test correlation measured on the archive of that rate (docs/method.md call 170)

notes.circularity: Scores are computed against the observed estimate with known standard error, not against the unknown true effect. This is the only option when no ground truth exists: the true effect of a past test is never observed, so a predictor can only be asked about the estimate the test produced.
notes.burn_in: Burn-in: the first scored origin has no earlier origin to build a reliability report from, so every row there abstains for 'reliability report is missing'. Abstention-adjusted figures for that origin are not comparable with later origins.
notes.abstention_triggers: All four triggers fired at least once. After the burn-in origin the reliability trigger fired on 0 rows, so no cell was marked drifted and every reliability abstention is the missing report at the burn-in origin.

rungs.P0: empirical base-rate forecaster of the visible ledger per cell: p_sig is the visible event rate, so its Brier skill is zero by construction
rungs.P1: empirical-Bayes prior per cell, pooled over kind of change and period
rungs.P2: weighted precedents (kernel regression on headline features) shrunk toward P1
rungs.always_reference: direction baseline: the reference arm wins (creation-order effect); direction accuracy only
rungs.always_variant: direction baseline: the variant wins; direction accuracy only

notes.p0_skill: P0 is the empirical base-rate forecaster: its significant-positive probability is the visible event rate of its cell, the same quantity the Brier skill is measured against, so its Brier skill is zero by construction and its calibration is a real out-of-time check of the base rate. A rung's Brier skill is always against that cell base rate, never against another rung.
notes.intervals: Three interval conventions are used. Every score interval is a 90 percent percentile bootstrap that resamples whole tests. The ECE percentile is read in a perfect-calibration null whose outcomes are drawn by test (contrasts of one test move together, with the within-test correlation estimated from the rows); 500 draws resolve percentiles up to 99.8, so 100 means above every draw. The gate simulation bootstraps by test and uses a 90 percent interval. Columns named adjusted_lo and adjusted_hi, and those ending in _adjusted_lo and _adjusted_hi, are Bonferroni-adjusted bounds for the family of intervals the table shows (the bootstrap standard error times the Bonferroni normal quantile); the per-cell and per-year intervals are descriptive.
notes.calibration_null: design_effect is the variance of the total residual with whole tests as the units over its independent-rows value; icc is the within-test correlation of the standardized residuals it implies and drives the clustered null. ece_percentile_independent is the percentile in the earlier null that draws every row independently, kept for comparison.
notes.decision_value: Random order captures K over n of the total by linearity, so it is exact, not a draw. A rung whose p_win is constant within a cell chooses by cell and then at random; its capture differs from random order only through between-cell differences. Intervals resample whole tests within each origin. The adjusted bounds are Bonferroni bounds for the family of rungs compared with random order in the pooled rows (family_size, the decision-value call of docs/method.md). diff_matched is the difference from random order matched to the arm-count composition of the chosen set, the baseline a rung must beat (the number of contrasts is known before launch).
notes.decidable_unit: the gates count tests, so decidable and decidable_research are the verdicts by tests (the same as decidable_by_tests and decidable_research_by_tests): a count of rows against gates sized in tests is not a decision
notes.cell_gate: The gate sizes are simulated at an archive-level rows per test and within-test correlation (gate_assumed_*). A cell has its own, measured on its rows (gate_cell_rows_per_test, gate_cell_icc); gate_cell_n_200 and gate_cell_n_400 scale the nearest simulated sizes to first order by the information a test carries, rows per test over the design effect, and decidable_by_tests_cell is the verdict at those sizes. A simulation per cell is too slow for the backtest path, so this is an approximation; decidable_by_tests stays the verdict at the nearest simulated row.
